title: Welcome to the ʿizba
goal: At Bū Rāshid's ʿizba in the desert outside Sharjah, with Rāshid there, he shows you his camels; ask about them and why the family keeps an ʿizba
tip: To ask about a way of life, kānaw + present says what people used to do: in-nās kānaw yishrabūn ḥalīb in-nāga. Ask about a family's habits with -ūn: shu tsawwūn fīhum? Bū Rāshid's camel words (il-bōsh, ḥuwār) are for recognition.
grammar: recycle: asking about a way of life (kānaw + present 'used to'; -ūn questions)
dialogue: A
حياك الله في عزبتنا يا ولدي. هذي العزبة ورثتها من أبوي
ḥayyāk allāh fi ʿizbatna yā wildi. hādhi l-ʿizba wiritht-ha min ubūy
Welcome to our ʿizba, son. I inherited this ʿizba from my father.
B
الله يحييك يا عمي. ما شاء الله، المكان كبير وايد
allāh yḥayyīk yā ʿammi. mā shāʼ allāh, il-makān kbīr wāyid
Thank you, uncle. Mā shāʼ allāh, it's a huge place.
A
وهذا البوش كله حقنا. نيي هني كل أسبوع في الشتا، وراشد يعطيهم العلف
w hādha l-bōsh killah ḥaggna. nyī hni kill usbūʿ fi sh-shita, w Rāshid yʿaṭīhum il-ʿalaf
And all these camels are ours. We come here every week in winter, and Rāshid gives them their feed.
B
كلهم حقكم؟ وشو تسوون فيهم؟
killhum ḥaggkum? w shu tsawwūn fīhum?
They're all yours? And what do you do with them?
A
هذي الناقة توها يابت حوار. وحليبها نشربه كل يوم الصبح
hādhi n-nāga tawwha yābat ḥuwār. w ḥalībha nishrabah kill yōm iṣ-ṣubḥ
This she-camel has just had a calf. And we drink her milk every morning.
B
حليب الناقة؟ عمري ما شربته!
ḥalīb in-nāga? ʿumri ma shribtah!
Camel milk? I've never had it!
A
ذوقه، ما في مثله. أهلنا في الماضي كانوا يشربونه كل يوم
dhūgah, ma fī mithlah. ahalna fi l-māẓi kānaw yishrabūnah kill yōm
Taste it; there's nothing like it. In the past our people used to drink it every day.
B
الله! حلو. بس ليش للحين عندكم عزبة، والبيت في الشارقة؟
allāh! ḥilu. bas lēsh lil-ḥīn ʿindakum ʿizba, w il-bēt fi sh-Shārja?
Wow, it's good. But why do you still have an ʿizba, when your home's in Sharjah?
A
عشان العيال ما ينسون التراث، ويعرفون كيف كانوا أهلهم يعيشون قبل النفط
ʿashān il-ʿyāl ma yinsūn it-turāth, w yaʿarfūn chēf kānaw ahalhum yʿīshūn gabil in-nafṭ
So the children don't forget the old ways, and know how their family lived before oil.
B
صدقت والله يا عمي. ممكن أشوفهم من قريب؟
ṣidagt wallāh yā ʿammi. mumkin ashūfhum min garīb?
You're so right, uncle. Can I see them up close?
items: the ʿizba (a family farm out in the desert, with camels and a majlis)
she's just had a calf (a camel)
culture: An ʿizba is a family farm out in the desert: camels, often goats and chickens, sometimes falcons, with a majlis and a kitchen, used as a desert holiday home. Families invite relatives and close friends there, so an invitation to the family ʿizba is a sign of trust.

title: A falcon on your hand
goal: At the ʿizba, Rāshid shows you his father's falcon; learn what its gear is called, and hold it on the glove for the first time
tip: Instructions come as short imperatives (ilbas il-mangala, irfaʿ īdak) and warnings as la + present (la titḥarrak wāyid). Ask permission with mumkin + an I-verb: mumkin ashīlah? The falconry words (il-burgaʿ, il-mangala, il-wakir, makhālbah) are for recognition.
grammar: recycle: instructions and warnings (imperatives; la + present)
dialogue: A
تعال شوف صقر أبوي، ييبه العزبة كل شتا. لا تخاف، عليه البرقع
taʿāl shūf ṣagr ubūy; yībah il-ʿizba kill shita. la tkhāf, ʿalēh il-burgaʿ
Come and see my dad's falcon; he brings him to the ʿizba every winter. Don't be scared: he's got his hood on.
B
ليش مغطين عيونه؟
lēsh mghaṭṭīn ʿyūnah?
Why have they covered his eyes?
A
عشان يكون هادي. إذا ما شاف شي، ما يخاف ولا يطير
ʿashān ykūn hādi. idha ma shāf shay, ma ykhāf wala yṭīr
So he stays calm. If he can't see anything, he doesn't get scared or fly off.
B
وهالشي اللي على إيدك شو؟
w hash-shay illi ʿala īdak shu?
And what's that thing on your hand?
A
هذي المنقلة. مخالبه قوية، وبدونها بيجرح إيدك
hādhi l-mangala. makhālbah gawiyya, w bidūnha biyijraḥ īdak
That's the glove. His talons are strong, and without it he'd cut your hand.
B
ممكن أشيله؟ بس ترا أول مرة
mumkin ashīlah? bas tara awwal marra
Can I hold him? It's my first time, though.
A
أكيد. البس المنقلة، وارفع إيدك شوي. ولا تتحرك وايد
akīd. ilbas il-mangala, w irfaʿ īdak shwayy. w la titḥarrak wāyid
Sure. Put the glove on and lift your hand a bit. And don't move too much.
B
أوه! شوف جناحه! وريشه ناعم وايد
ōh! shūf jināḥah! w rīshah nāʿim wāyid
Oh! Look at his wing! And his feathers are so soft.
A
شفت؟ ارتاح عليك. بعدين نرجعه على الوكر، وتصير صقار مثل أبوي!
shift? irtāḥ ʿalēk. baʿdēn nrajjʿah ʿala l-wakir, w tṣīr ṣaggār mithil ubūy!
See? He's settled on you. Afterwards we'll put him back on his perch, and you'll be a falconer like my dad!
B
مرة وحدة؟ خلني أتعلم أشيله زين أول! هذا تراث، مب لعبة
marra waḥda? khallni atʿallam ashīlah zēn awwal! hādha turāth, mub liʿba
Just like that? Let me learn to hold him properly first! This is heritage, not a game.
items: your dad's falcon: ṣagr ubūk (صقر أبوك)
he's got his hood on (a falcon)
(recognise); il-burgaʿ is also the face mask some older Emirati women wear
culture: Falconry is part of Emirati heritage: in 2010 the UAE led a group of countries in having it added to UNESCO's list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity. The leather hood (il-burgaʿ) covers the falcon's eyes to keep it calm, and it rests on the falconer's glove (il-mangala) or on a wooden perch (il-wakir) pushed into the sand.

title: Bint il-barg: truffles after the rain
goal: Out in the desert after the winter rain with your classmate Mājid, look for desert truffles the way his uncle taught him, and keep the spot to yourselves
tip: Guess from what you see with yimkin ('maybe') and shaklah ('it looks like it'): yimkin tiḥtah shay? – shaklah! Mājid's words for the truffles (il-fagʿ, bint il-barg) are for recognition; to tell him you've found one, ligēt shay! is enough.
grammar: recycle: guessing from signs (yimkin, shaklah, idha …)
dialogue: A
شوف البر كيف صار أخضر بعد المطر! طلع العشب في كل مكان، وهذا شي نادر
shūf il-barr chēf ṣār akhẓar baʿd il-maṭar! ṭilaʿ il-ʿushub fi kill makān, w hādha shay nādir
Look how green the desert's turned after the rain! The grass has come up everywhere, and that's rare.
B
ما شاء الله! عمري ما شفته جي. شو ندور بالضبط؟
mā shāʼ allāh! ʿumri ma shiftah chī. shu ndawwir biẓ-ẓabṭ?
Mā shāʼ allāh! I've never seen it like this. What are we looking for, exactly?
A
الفقع. خالي يقول يطلع بعد المطر اللي فيه رعد وبرق
il-fagʿ. khāli ygūl yiṭlaʿ baʿd il-maṭar illi fīh raʿd w barg
Desert truffles. My uncle says they come up after rain with thunder and lightning.
B
وشلون نعرف وين هو؟ أكيد تحت الأرض
w shlōn naʿarf wēn huwa? akīd taḥt il-arẓ
And how do we know where they are? They must be underground.
A
هيه، ينبت تحت الأرض. تدور شق صغير، والأماكن سر، محد يقولها لك
hē, yinbit taḥt il-arẓ. tdawwir shagg ṣghīr, w il-amākin sirr, maḥḥad ygūlha-lak
Yes, they grow underground. You look for a little crack, and the spots are a secret: nobody tells you them.
B
هني! شوف هالشق. يمكن تحته شي؟
hni! shūf hash-shagg. yimkin tiḥtah shay?
Here! Look at this crack. Maybe there's something under it?
A
شكله! بس شوي شوي، دور بإيدك
shaklah! bas shwayy shwayy, dawwir b-īdak
Looks like it! But gently: feel around with your hand.
B
لقيت شي! أبيض وكبير
ligēt shay! abyaẓ w kbīr
I've found something! It's white and big.
A
ما شاء الله عليك! أهلنا يسمونه بنت البرق، وكان رزقهم في الشتا
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk! ahalna ysammūnah bint il-barg, w kān rizghum fi sh-shita
Well done! Our old folk call it 'daughter of the lightning', and it was what they lived on in winter.
B
حلو الاسم. والمكان؟ بيني وبينك!
ḥilu l-isim. w il-makān? bēni w bēnak!
What a lovely name. And the spot? Just between you and me!
items: a feminine thing: ṣārat khaẓra (صارت خضرا)
'daughter of the lightning' (an old name for desert truffles)

title: Poetry in the majlis
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, with Rāshid there, a guest has just recited a nabaṭi poem; say how much you understood, and ask Bū Rāshid what nabaṭi poetry is
tip: Say honestly how much you followed: simaʿt-ha, bas ma fhimt killha. Then check with yaʿni …?: yaʿni mithil il-amthāl? Bū Rāshid's words for the poetry (shiʿir nabaṭi, il-ḥanīn, il-furūsiyya) are for recognition.
grammar: recycle: saying how much you understood (ma fhimt killha, bas …; yaʿni …?)
dialogue: A
سمعت القصيدة يا سالم؟ هذا شعر نبطي، شعر البدو
simaʿt il-gaṣīda yā Sālim? hādha shiʿir nabaṭi, shiʿir il-badu
Did you hear the poem, Sālim? That's nabaṭi poetry, the poetry of the Bedouin.
B
سمعتها، بس ما فهمت كلها. الكلمات قديمة وايد
simaʿt-ha, bas ma fhimt killha. il-kalimāt gadīma wāyid
I heard it, but I didn't understand all of it. The words are very old.
A
النبطي باللهجة، مب بالفصحى. بس فيه كلمات من الماضي، ما يستخدمونها الشباب الحين
in-nabaṭi bil-lahja, mub bil-fuṣḥa. bas fīh kalimāt min il-māẓi, ma yistakhdmūnha sh-shabāb il-ḥīn
Nabaṭi is in the dialect, not in fuṣḥā. But it has words from the past that young people don't use now.
B
وعن شو كانت القصيدة؟
w ʿan shu kānat il-gaṣīda?
And what was the poem about?
A
عن الصحرا، والحنين للأهل. وفي قصايد عن الفروسية والحكمة
ʿan iṣ-ṣaḥra, w il-ḥanīn lil-ahal. w fī gaṣāyid ʿan il-furūsiyya w il-ḥikma
About the desert, and longing for family. And there are poems about chivalry and wisdom.
B
يعني مثل الأمثال؟ كل بيت فيه حكمة؟
yaʿni mithil il-amthāl? kill bēt fīh ḥikma?
So it's like proverbs? Every line has some wisdom in it?
A
مرات. والبدو أيام أول كانوا ينظمون الشعر عن كل شي في حياتهم، حتى الألغاز. هذا تراثنا
marrāt. w il-badu ayyām awwal kānaw yinẓimūn ish-shiʿir ʿan kill shay fi ḥayāt-hum, ḥatta l-alghāz. hādha turāthna
Sometimes. And in the old days the Bedouin composed poetry about everything in their lives, even riddles. That's our heritage.
B
والحين؟ الشباب يحبونه بعد؟
w il-ḥīn? ish-shabāb yḥibbūnah baʿad?
And today? Do young people like it too?
A
هيه، في مسابقات في التلفزيون، وراشد يتابعها ويايه في العزبة كل أسبوع
hē, fī musābagāt fi t-tilfizyōn, w Rāshid ytābiʿha wiyyāy fi l-ʿizba kill usbūʿ
Yes, there are competitions on TV, and Rāshid watches them with me at the ʿizba every week.
B
عيل بتابعها معكم. يمكن أفهم بيت أو بيتين!
ʿayal batābiʿha maʿakum. yimkin afham bēt aw bētēn!
Then I'll watch with you. Maybe I'll understand a line or two!
items: the desert (the open desert, in poems and stories)
nabaṭi poetry (Bedouin poetry in the dialect)
chivalry, horsemanship (a theme of old poems)
culture: Nabaṭi poetry began among the Bedouin of the Arabian Peninsula and is composed in the spoken dialect, not classical Arabic. Its themes include chivalry, pride, longing, advice and wisdom, love of family and country, and the desert. It has had a revival in the UAE, helped by televised poetry competitions watched across the Gulf.

title: The desert misses you, Sēf
goal: On a video call from abroad, Sēf sees your photos from his uncle's ʿizba; tell him about it, tease him about the cold, and plan his next visit home
tip: Tell news in short past-tense bursts, one thing per sentence: shilt iṣ-ṣagr ʿala īdi! w shribt ḥalīb in-nāga. Friends tease about luck and weather: yā ḥaẓẓak!, aḥsidak! 'I'm jealous!'. Plan with yōm + present: yōm tirjaʿ 'when you're back'.
grammar: recycle: telling a friend about your weekend (past narrative; la … wala)
dialogue: A
هلا والله! شو هالصور اللي طرشتها؟ صقر وبوش وفقع!
hala wallāh! shu haṣ-ṣuwar illi ṭarrasht-ha? ṣagr w bōsh w fagʿ!
Hey! What are these photos you sent? A falcon, camels and truffles!
B
هلا فيك! كنا في عزبة عمك ويا راشد
hala fīk! kinna fi ʿizbat ʿammak wiyya Rāshid
Hi! We were at your uncle's ʿizba with Rāshid.
A
يا حظك! أنا هني لا بر ولا عزبة، بس ضباب وبرد
yā ḥaẓẓak! ana hni la barr wala ʿizba, bas ẓabāb w bard
Lucky you! Here I've got no desert and no ʿizba, just fog and cold.
B
شلت الصقر على إيدي أول مرة! وشربت حليب الناقة
shilt iṣ-ṣagr ʿala īdi awwal marra! w shribt ḥalīb in-nāga
I held the falcon on my hand for the first time! And I drank camel milk.
A
والله أحسدك! أنا قاعد أرجف من البرد
wallāh aḥsidak! ana gāʿid arjif min il-bard
Honestly, I'm jealous! I'm sitting here shivering from the cold.
B
مسكين! وأنا هني في الدفا، والبر أخضر بعد المطر
maskīn! w ana hni fi d-dafa, w il-barr akhẓar baʿd il-maṭar
Poor you! And I'm here in the warm, and the desert's green after the rain.
A
لا تزيدها علي! صج متجمد، ما أحس بإيدي
la tzīdha ʿalay! ṣij mitjammid, ma aḥiss b-īdi
Don't rub it in! I'm really frozen; I can't feel my hands.
B
عيل يوم ترجع في الإجازة، أول شي العزبة
ʿayal yōm tirjaʿ fi l-ijāza, awwal shay il-ʿizba
Then when you're back for the holidays, the ʿizba's the first thing.
A
اتفقنا! ويدي، الله يرحمه، كان يقول شعر في العزبة
ittafagna! w yaddi, allāh yirḥamah, kān ygūl shiʿir fi l-ʿizba
Deal! And my grandad, God rest his soul, used to recite poetry at the ʿizba.
B
آمين، الله يرحمه. عيل لازم تعلمني شوي منه
āmīn, allāh yirḥamah. ʿayal lāzim tʿallimni shwayy minnah
Amen, God rest his soul. Then you've got to teach me a bit of it.
items: to a woman: yā ḥaẓẓich (يا حظج)
I'm jealous! (teasing, among friends) (to a man)
to a woman: aḥsidich (أحسدج); friends only: said as a joke
in the warm, where it's warm
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner, have a 10-minute conversation about desert life. Ask what they know about camels, falconry and the ʿizba, and tell them about a trip of your own in past-tense bursts (shilt…, shribt…). To prepare, search YouTube for «الصقارة» (falconry) or «يوم في العزبة» (a day at the ʿizba), and note three words you hear.

title: What was the sermon about?
goal: Outside the mosque in Sharjah after the Friday prayer, with Rāshid there, ask Bū Rāshid about the fuṣḥā phrases you heard in the sermon
tip: The sermon is in fuṣḥā, but you talk about it in Gulf Arabic: il-khuṭba l-yōm kānat ʿan iz-zakā. The preacher's set phrases (ʿibād allāh, ittaqu llāh, aqūlu qawli hādha …) are for recognition; Bū Rāshid explains each one with yaʿni.
grammar: fuṣḥā bridge: recognising set phrases from the sermon, explaining them in Gulf
dialogue: A
تقبل الله يا ولدي
tagabbal allāh yā wildi
May God accept (your prayer), son.
B
منا ومنكم يا عمي. الخطبة اليوم كانت عن الزكاة، صح؟
minna w minkum yā ʿammi. il-khuṭba l-yōm kānat ʿan iz-zakā, ṣaḥḥ?
From us and from you, uncle. Today's sermon was about zakat, wasn't it?
A
صح، عشان رمضان قريب. والخطيب قرا آية عن الزكاة، وهذا خطيب نادر، كلامه واضح. فهمته؟
ṣaḥḥ, ʿashān ramaẓān garīb. w il-khaṭīb gara āya ʿan iz-zakā; hādha khaṭīb nādir, kalāmah wāẓiḥ. fhimtah?
Right, because Ramadan's coming. And the preacher recited a verse about zakat; he's a rare preacher, he speaks clearly. Did you follow him?
B
شوي. الفصحى في الخطبة صعبة علي
shwayy. il-fuṣḥa fi l-khuṭba ṣaʿba ʿalay
A bit. The fuṣḥā in the sermon is hard for me.
A
أول ما طلع المنبر قال «عباد الله، اتقوا الله»، يعني يا ناس، خافوا الله في كل شي
awwal ma ṭilaʿ il-minbar gāl “ʿibād allāh, ittaqu llāh”, yaʿni yā nās, khāfu llāh fi kill shay
As soon as he went up the minbar he said 'servants of God, fear God': it means, people, be mindful of God in everything.
B
وليش يقعد في النص، بين الخطبتين؟
w lēsh yigʿid fi n-nuṣṣ, bēn il-khuṭbatēn?
And why does he sit down in the middle, between the two sermons?
A
هذا من السنة. النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يخطب خطبتين، ويقعد بينهم، وهو قدوتنا
hādha min is-sunna. in-nabi ṣalla llāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam kān yikhṭub khuṭbatēn, w yigʿid bēnhum, w huwa gidwatna
That's from the Sunna. The Prophet, peace be upon him, used to give two sermons and sit between them, and he's our example.
B
وفي آخر الخطبة الأولى، شو قال؟
w fi ākhir il-khuṭba l-ūla, shu gāl?
And at the end of the first sermon, what did he say?
A
«أقول قولي هذا وأستغفر الله العظيم لي ولكم». يعني خلصت كلامي، والله يغفر لنا كلنا
“aqūlu qawli hādha wa astaghfiru llāha l-ʿaẓīma li wa lakum”. yaʿni khallaṣt kalāmi, w allāh yighfir lana killana
'I say these words of mine and ask God Almighty's forgiveness for me and for you.' It means: I've finished, and may God forgive us all.
B
الحين فهمت! يا حظك يا راشد، انت تفهم كل شي
il-ḥīn fhimt! yā ḥaẓẓak yā Rāshid, inta tifham kill shay
Now I get it! Lucky you, Rāshid: you understand all of it.
items: zakat (the alms a Muslim with enough savings must pay each year)
he recited a verse (of the Quran)
servants of God, fear God (formal, from the sermon)
he went up the minbar (the mosque's pulpit)
from the Sunna (what the Prophet did)
culture: The Friday sermon (khuṭba) is given in fuṣḥā from the minbar before the prayer, in two parts, with the preacher sitting briefly between them, as the Prophet did. It often opens with 'servants of God, fear God', and the first part often ends with 'I say these words of mine and ask God's forgiveness for me and for you'.

title: Do I owe zakat?
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis in Ramadan, with Rāshid there, ask him whether you owe zakat on your internship savings, and check what you've understood
tip: Check you've understood by saying it back with yaʿni: yaʿni min kill alf, khamsa w ʿishrīn? Ask about a duty with lāzim …? 'do I have to …?'. Bū Rāshid's religious terms (sana hijriyya, il-bukhul) are for recognition.
grammar: recycle: asking for advice and checking (idha …, yaʿni …?, ṣaḥḥ?)
dialogue: B
يا عمي، الخطيب قرا آية عن الزكاة. عندي سؤال
yā ʿammi, il-khaṭīb gara āya ʿan iz-zakā. ʿindi suʼāl
Uncle, the preacher recited a verse about zakat. I've got a question.
A
تفضل يا ولدي، اسأل
tfaẓẓal yā wildi, isʼal
Go ahead, son, ask.
B
رصيدي في البنك من التدريب صار له سنة. لازم أدفع زكاته؟
riṣīdi fi l-bank min it-tadrīb ṣār-lah sana. lāzim adfaʿ zakātah?
My bank balance from the internship has been there a year. Do I have to pay zakat on it?
A
إذا وصل النصاب، وكمل عندك سنة هجرية، هيه لازم
idha wiṣal in-niṣāb, w kimal ʿindak sana hijriyya, hē lāzim
If it's reached the niṣāb, the minimum, and you've had it a full Hijri year, then yes, you do.
B
والنصاب كم؟
w in-niṣāb cham?
And how much is the niṣāb?
A
على حسب سعر الذهب، يعني يتغير. وتدفع ربع العشر، يعني ثنين ونص بالمية
ʿala ḥasab siʿir idh-dhahab, yaʿni yitghayyar. w tidfaʿ rubʿ il-ʿushur, yaʿni thnēn w nuṣṣ bil-miya
It goes by the price of gold, so it changes. And you pay a quarter of a tenth, that's two and a half per cent.
B
يعني من كل ألف، خمسة وعشرين؟
yaʿni min kill alf, khamsa w ʿishrīn?
So out of every thousand, twenty-five?
A
بالضبط. وتعطيها الفقير والمحتاج، والأيتام. هذا تعاون بين الناس
biẓ-ẓabṭ. w tʿaṭīha l-fagīr w il-miḥtāj, w il-aytām. hādha taʿāwun bēn in-nās
Exactly. And you give it to the poor and the needy, and to orphans. It's people helping each other.
B
ما كنت أدري إنها جي واضحة
ma kint adri innha chī wāẓḥa
I didn't know it was this clear.
A
والزكاة تبعد الواحد عن البخل، وتبارك في المال
w iz-zakā tibʿid il-wāḥid ʿan il-bukhul, w tbārik fi l-māl
And zakat keeps a man away from meanness, and brings blessing to his money.
items: my bank balance, my savings in the bank
culture: Zakat on savings is 2.5 per cent of wealth that has stayed at or above the niṣāb, a minimum set by the value of 87.48 grams of gold, for a full lunar year. It can be paid at any time of year, but many people pay it in Ramadan.

title: Longer than Ramadan! Fahad's sayings
goal: On a video call from Kuwait during Ramadan, Fahad teaches you three Kuwaiti sayings about Ramadan; work out what each one means and when you'd use it
tip: When you hear a saying, check how it's used: tgūlūnha ʿan …? 'do you say it about …?', or yaʿni …? Fahad's Kuwaiti sayings, and his ghabga, are for recognition. Answer news of someone poor with allāh yiʿīnah.
grammar: recycle: checking what a saying means (tgūlūnha ʿan …?, yaʿni …?)
dialogue: A
هلا والله! شلونك؟ شلون الصيام عندكم؟
hala wallāh! shlōnak? shlōn iṣ-ṣiyām ʿindakum?
Hey! How are you? How's the fasting going over there?
B
هلا فيك! زين الحمد لله، بس العطش صعب في الدوام
hala fīk! zēn il-ḥamdu lillāh, bas il-ʿaṭash ṣaʿb fi d-dawām
Hi! Fine, thank God, but the thirst is hard at work.
A
لازم تشرب ماي وايد في السحور. وعندنا في الكويت نقول عن الشي الصعب «أطول من شهر رمضان»
lāzim tishrab māy wāyid fi s-saḥūr. w ʿindana fi l-Kwēt ngūl ʿan ish-shay iṣ-ṣaʿb “aṭwal min shahar ramaẓān”
You need to drink lots of water at suhoor. And in Kuwait we say of something hard, 'longer than the month of Ramadan'.
B
حلوة! تقولونها عن أي شي صعب؟
ḥilwa! tgūlūnha ʿan ay shay ṣaʿb?
Nice! Do you say it about anything hard?
A
إيه. وعن الشي اللي لازم تسويه نقول «أفرض من الصوم والصلاة»
ēh. w ʿan ish-shay illi lāzim tsawwīh ngūl “afraẓ min iṣ-ṣōm w iṣ-ṣalā”
Yes. And for something you absolutely have to do, we say 'more of a duty than fasting and prayer'.
B
يعني مثل السحور!
yaʿni mithil is-saḥūr!
So, like suhoor!
A
ههه، بالضبط! وعن الفقير والمحتاج يقولون «ما عنده ما يفطر الصايم»
hhh, biẓ-ẓabṭ! w ʿan il-fagīr w il-miḥtāj ygūlūn “ma ʿindah ma yfaṭṭir iṣ-ṣāyim”
Ha, exactly! And about the poor and needy they say 'he hasn't enough to feed a fasting man'.
B
الله يعينه. عشان جي الزكاة والصدقة في رمضان لها أجر كبير
allāh yiʿīnah. ʿashān chī z-zakā w iṣ-ṣadaga fi ramaẓān laha ajir kbīr
God help him. That's why zakat and charity in Ramadan bring a great reward.
A
صدقت. والليلة عندنا غبقة في البيت، بعد التراويح، للأهل والييران، وأمي بتطرش أكل للأيتام
ṣidagt. w il-lēla ʿindana ghabga fi l-bēt, baʿd it-tarāwīḥ, lil-ahal w il-yīrān, w ummi bitṭarrish akil lil-aytām
You're right. And tonight we've got a ghabga at home after tarāwīḥ, for family and neighbours, and my mum's sending food to orphans.
B
ما شاء الله! سلم لي عليهم كلهم
mā shāʼ allāh! sallim-li ʿalēhum killhum
Mā shāʼ allāh! Say hi to them all from me.
items: suhoor (the meal before dawn in Ramadan)
'longer than the month of Ramadan' (said of something hard) (Kuwait)
'more of a duty than fasting and prayer' (something you must do) (Kuwait)
'he can't even feed a fasting man' (said of someone very poor) (Kuwait)
لا يملك ما يفطر به الصائم
a ghabga (a late-evening Ramadan meal for family and neighbours) (Kuwait)
culture: These three sayings are recorded as Kuwaiti Ramadan proverbs: 'longer than the month of Ramadan' is said of something hard, 'more of a duty than fasting and prayer' of something that must be done, and 'he hasn't enough to feed a fasting man' of real poverty. A ghabga is a meal held after the tarāwīḥ prayers in Ramadan for family and neighbours.

title: A water cooler for Grandad
goal: After the night prayer in Ramadan, Rāshid shows you the water cooler his father put up outside the mosque for his late grandfather; talk about lasting charity
tip: ʿan rūḥ + a person says who a good deed is done for after their death: ʿan rūḥ yaddi. Add what it does with a present verb: tisgi l-ʿaṭshān 'it gives the thirsty a drink'. The hadith wording (ʿilm yuntafaʿu bih, yaghrisu gharsan) is fuṣḥā, for recognition.
grammar: recycle: explaining a purpose (ʿan rūḥ …, ʿashān …, yaʿni …)
dialogue: B
هالبرادة يديدة؟ ما كانت هني قبل
hal-barrāda yidīda? ma kānat hni gabil
Is this water cooler new? It wasn't here before.
A
هيه، أبوي حطها عن روح يدي، الله يرحمه. يقول هذي صدقة جارية، ومن التراث بعد
hē, ubūy ḥaṭṭha ʿan rūḥ yaddi, allāh yirḥamah. ygūl hādhi ṣadaga jārya, w min it-turāth baʿad
Yes, my dad put it up for my late grandad, God rest his soul. He says it's a charity that goes on, and part of our heritage too.
B
آمين، الله يرحمه. يعني كل واحد يشرب منها، يدك ياخذ أجر؟
āmīn, allāh yirḥamah. yaʿni kill wāḥid yishrab minha, yaddak yākhidh ajir?
Amen, God rest his soul. So everyone who drinks from it, your grandad gets a reward?
A
إن شاء الله. تسقي العطشان في الحر، والثواب يوصله كل يوم
in shāʼ allāh. tisgi l-ʿaṭshān fi l-ḥarr, w ith-thawāb yōṣlah kill yōm
God willing. It gives the thirsty a drink in the heat, and the reward reaches him every day.
B
حلوة وايد. وغير الزكاة، في أشياء ثانية؟
ḥilwa wāyid. w ghēr iz-zakā, fī ashyāʼ thānya?
That's lovely. And apart from zakat, are there other things?
A
وايد. في الحديث: «صدقة جارية، أو علم ينتفع به، أو ولد صالح يدعو له»
wāyid. fi l-ḥadīth: “ṣadaqa jāriya, aw ʿilm yuntafaʿu bih, aw walad ṣāliḥ yadʿū lah”
Lots. In the hadith: 'an ongoing charity, or knowledge that benefits people, or a righteous child who prays for him'.
B
وانت الولد اللي يدعي له!
w inta l-walad illi yidʿī-lah!
And you're the boy who prays for him!
A
إن شاء الله. وفي حديث ثاني: اللي «يغرس غرسا»، ياكل منه طير أو إنسان، له صدقة
in shāʼ allāh. w fī ḥadīth thāni: illi “yaghrisu gharsan”, yākil minnah ṭēr aw insān, lah ṣadaga
God willing. And in another hadith: whoever 'plants a plant' that a bird or a person eats from, it counts as charity for him.
B
عيل بزرع نخلة عند البيت!
ʿayal bazraʿ nakhla ʿind il-bēt!
Then I'll plant a palm tree by the house!
A
صدقت! أبوي بيستانس، وبنزرع وحدة في العزبة باسم يدي
ṣidagt! ubūy biystānis, w binizraʿ waḥda fi l-ʿizba b-ism yaddi
Good thinking! My dad will be pleased, and we'll plant one at the ʿizba in my grandad's name.
items: an ongoing charity (a good deed whose reward goes on after death)
it (f.) gives the thirsty a drink
the reward (from God, for a good deed)
knowledge that benefits people (formal, from the hadith)
he plants a plant (formal, from the hadith)
culture: An ongoing charity (ṣadaqa jāriya) is one whose good goes on after death. A hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim says a person's deeds end at death except for three: an ongoing charity, knowledge that benefits others, and a righteous child who prays for them. Another, in al-Bukhārī, says a plant that a bird or a person eats from counts as charity.

title: Before the Eid prayer
goal: At the office in the last days of Ramadan, with the team around, Maryam asks whether you've paid zakāt il-fiṭr; check the rules with her and how you can pay
tip: Say what's required with lāzim gabil … and what's possible with tigdar … aw … 'you can … or …'. To a woman, B says innich and dhakkartīni 'you (f.) reminded me'. Zakāt il-fiṭr and awwal shawwāl are for recognition.
grammar: recycle: duties and options (lāzim gabil …, tigdar … aw …)
dialogue: A
سالم، دفعت زكاة الفطر ولّا بعدك؟
Sālim, difaʿt zakāt il-fiṭr walla baʿdak?
Sālim, have you paid zakāt il-fiṭr, or not yet?
B
بعدني. لازم قبل صلاة العيد، صح؟
baʿadni. lāzim gabil ṣalāt il-ʿīd, ṣaḥḥ?
Not yet. It has to be before the Eid prayer, right?
A
هيه، قبل الصلاة يوم أول شوال. وعن كل فرد في البيت، حتى العيال
hē, gabil iṣ-ṣalā yōm awwal shawwāl. w ʿan kill fard fi l-bēt, ḥatta l-ʿyāl
Yes, before the prayer on the first of Shawwāl. And for every person in the household, even the children.
B
أنا ساكن ويا ربيعي، يعني عن نفسي بس، صح؟
ana sākin wiyya rbīʿi, yaʿni ʿan nafsi bas, ṣaḥḥ?
I live with a friend, so just for myself, right?
A
زين. أيام النبي كانت «صاعا من تمر»، والحين تقدر تعطيها كيلوين ونص عيش، أو فلوس
zēn. ayyām in-nabi kānat “ṣāʿan min tamr”, w il-ḥīn tigdar tʿaṭīha kīlōyn w nuṣṣ ʿēsh, aw flūs
Fine. In the Prophet's day it was 'a ṣāʿ of dates'; now you can give two and a half kilos of rice, or money.
B
وأعطيها منو؟ ما أعرف حد محتاج
w aʿaṭīha minu? ma aʿarf ḥad miḥtāj
And who do I give it to? I don't know anyone in need.
A
الجمعيات الخيرية تاخذها، ويوزعونها على المحتاجين والأيتام قبل العيد
il-jamʿiyyāt il-khēriyya tākhidhha, w ywazzʿūnha ʿala l-miḥtājīn w il-aytām gabil il-ʿīd
The charities take it, and they hand it out to people in need and orphans before Eid.
B
زين. وغير الزكاة، أبي أتبرع بشي بعد، صدقة جارية
zēn. w ghēr iz-zakā, abi atbarraʿ b-shay baʿad, ṣadaga jārya
Good. And apart from zakat, I'd like to donate something too, an ongoing charity.
A
التبرع ما له وقت، متى ما تبي. بس زكاة الفطر لها وقت
it-tabarruʿ ma lah wagt, mita ma tabi. bas zakāt il-fiṭr laha wagt
Donating has no set time: whenever you like. But zakāt il-fiṭr has its time.
B
زين إنج ذكرتيني! باكر الصبح بدفعها إن شاء الله
zēn innich dhakkartīni! bāchir iṣ-ṣubḥ badfaʿha in shāʼ allāh
Good thing you reminded me! I'll pay it tomorrow morning, God willing.
items: two and a half kilos of rice
for each person, for every individual
a ṣāʿ (an old measure) of dates (formal, from the hadith)
(to) donate something, give something to charity
zakāt il-fiṭr (the alms paid for each person before the Eid prayer)
the first of Shawwāl (the day of Eid al-Fiṭr)
culture: Zakāt il-fiṭr is paid for every Muslim in the household, children included, and must be paid before the Eid prayer. It is usually reckoned as about 2.5 kg of rice per person, and in the UAE it may also be paid in cash; the amount in money is announced each year.
task: This week: search YouTube for «خطبة الجمعة» (Friday sermon). It is in fuṣḥā, so expect no dialect. Listen to the first three minutes twice and note each set phrase you know (عباد الله, اتقوا الله, أقول قولي هذا). Then tell Bū Rāshid, in respectful Gulf Arabic and in five sentences, what the sermon was about (il-khuṭba kānat ʿan …).

title: Checkpoint 5.5: Eid at the majlis
goal: Checkpoint: on Eid morning in Bū Rāshid's majlis, Sēf, home for the Eid holiday, catches up on your Ramadan and plans the ʿizba for the holiday
tip: This checkpoint recycles the block: the ʿizba and its camels, the falcon, the sermon, zakāt il-fiṭr and charity. Answer an Eid greeting by saying it back: ʿasākum min ʿuwwādah. Say you'd love to with wallāh widdi!
grammar: checkpoint 5.5 (s5u065–s5u080): heritage words, the sermon, zakat and charity
dialogue: A
عساكم من عواده يا سالم!
ʿasākum min ʿuwwādah yā Sālim!
Eid Mubarak, Sālim! (lit. may you live to see it come back)
B
عساكم من عواده! الحمد لله على السلامة
ʿasākum min ʿuwwādah! il-ḥamdu lillāh ʿala s-salāma
Eid Mubarak! Welcome home, Sēf.
A
الله يسلمك. شفت الهلال البارحة؟ ما توقعنا العيد اليوم!
allāh ysallmak. shift il-hilāl il-bārḥa? ma twaggaʿna l-ʿīd il-yōm!
Thank you. Did you see the new moon last night? We didn't expect Eid today!
B
لا. بس دفعت زكاة الفطر قبل الصلاة
la. bas difaʿt zakāt il-fiṭr gabil iṣ-ṣalā
No. But I paid zakāt il-fiṭr before the prayer.
A
ما شاء الله عليك! وعمي يقول دفعت زكاتك بعد
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk! w ʿammi ygūl difaʿt zakātak baʿad
Well done! And my uncle says you paid your zakat too.
B
هيه، هو اللي شرح لي. وأبوك زرع نخلة باسم يدك
hē, huwa illi sharaḥ-li. w ubūk zaraʿ nakhla b-ism yaddak
Yes, he's the one who explained it to me. And your dad planted a palm tree in your grandad's name.
A
الله يرحمه. وثاني يوم العيد بنروح العزبة، نشوف الإبل ونسوي لقيمات على الجمر
allāh yirḥamah. w thāni yōm il-ʿīd binrūḥ il-ʿizba, nshūf il-ibil w nsawwi lgēmāt ʿala l-jamir
God rest his soul. And on the second day of Eid we'll go to the ʿizba, see the camels and make luqaimat over the embers.
B
آمين، الله يرحمه. والله ودي! بس هالمرة أنا اللي بشيل الصقر
āmīn, allāh yirḥamah. wallāh widdi! bas hal-marra ana illi bashīl iṣ-ṣagr
Amen, God rest his soul. I'd love to! But this time I'm the one holding the falcon.
A
خلاص، وأنا أشرب حليب الناقة. وعمي بيطلع الشاهين اليديد، وراشد بيقول لنا شعر نبطي!
khalāṣ, w ana ashrab ḥalīb in-nāga. w ʿammi biyṭalliʿ ish-shāhīn il-yidīd, w Rāshid biygūl-lana shiʿir nabaṭi!
Done, and I'll drink the camel milk. And my uncle's bringing out his new peregrine, and Rāshid's going to recite nabaṭi poetry for us!
B
عيل بنسمعه للآخر، حتى لو ما فهمنا!
ʿayal binismaʿah lil-ākhir, ḥatta lō ma fhimna!
Then we'll listen to the end, even if we don't understand!
items: the new moon, the crescent (that starts the month)
camels (the general word, as in the news)
over the embers, on the coals
luqaimat (sweet fried dough balls with date syrup)
(recognise); the falcon most used for hunting: il-ḥurr (الحر)
